answer_surfaces.answer_text: Diffusion is a passive process in which a single substance moves from a high-concentration area to a low-concentration area until concentration is equal across a space [ev_008], and it expends no energy [ev_009]. Osmosis is a special case of diffusion [ev_001]: it is the movement of free water molecules through a semipermeable membrane down the water's concentration gradient, which is inversely proportional to the solutes' concentration [ev_001]. The key difference is scope: diffusion transports material across membranes and within cells, whereas osmosis transports only water across a membrane, and the membrane limits the solutes' diffusion in the water [ev_001].
answer_surfaces.short_answer: Diffusion moves a substance from high to low concentration until equal, expending no energy [ev_008] [ev_009]; osmosis is a special case of diffusion in which only water moves through a semipermeable membrane down its own concentration gradient, which is inversely proportional to solute concentration [ev_001].

answer_surfaces.answer_text: No. Osmosis transports only water across a membrane, and the membrane limits the diffusion of solutes in the water [ev_002] [ev_003]. Solutes can move across membranes by other means, such as facilitated diffusion through transport proteins, but that is not osmosis [ev_002]. In the osmosis setup, the solute cannot pass through the selectively permeable membrane, while the water can [ev_004].

J02:F007.exact_text: Facilitated transport In facilitated transport, also called facilitated diffusion, material moves across the plasma membrane with the assistance of transmembrane proteins down a concentration gradient (from high to low concentration) without the expenditure of cellular energy.

J02:F013.exact_text: The integral proteins involved in facilitated transport are collectively referred to as transport proteins, and they function as either channels for the material or carriers.

J02:F023.exact_text: FIGURE 3.21 In osmosis, water always moves from an area of higher concentration (of water) to one of lower concentration (of water). In this system, the solute cannot pass through the selectively permeable membrane. A principle of diffusion is that the molecules move around and will spread evenly throughout the medium if they can. However, only the material capable of getting through the membrane will diffuse through it. In this example, the solute cannot diffuse through the membrane, but the water can. Water has a concentration gradient in this system. Therefore, water will diffuse down its concentration gradient, crossing the membrane to the side where it is less concentrated. This diffusion of water through the membrane—osmosis—will continue until the concentration gradient of water goes to zero. Osmosis proceeds constantly in living systems.
